Recurrent Sore Throat? It May Be More Than Just an Infection
Do you or your child frequently suffer from sore throats, tonsillitis, snoring, or bad breath?
Enlarged or infected tonsils can cause repeated throat infections, difficulty swallowing, sleep disturbances, and even obstructive sleep apnoea.

Common warning signs include:
. Recurrent throat infections
. Persistent bad breath (tonsil stones)
. Difficulty swallowing
. Loud snoring or mouth breathing
. Enlarged tonsils
.Symptoms lasting more than 2–3 weeks
Not all sore throats need antibiotics. An ENT evaluation can help identify whether the cause is viral, bacterial, allergic, reflux-related, or due to tonsil disease.
If you or your child experience recurrent symptoms, seek timely assessment.

Ear Infections and Ear Pain: When Should You See an ENT Specialist? BY Dr Sheetal Radia,ENT specialist ,Mulund ,Bhandup& Thane.

Ear pain is one of the most common reasons patients visit an ENT clinic. While some ear infections are mild and resolve quickly, others can lead to hearing loss, recurrent infections, and complications if left untreated.

What Causes Ear Pain?
Ear pain can originate from:
. Outer ear infections (Swimmer's Ear)
.Middle ear infections (Otitis Media)
. Earwax blockage
. Eardrum injury
. Sinus infections and allergies
.Throat infections
.Dental problems
. Air travel pressure changes (Barotrauma)

Sometimes the ear itself may be normal, and pain may be referred from the throat, nose, jaw, or teeth.
